title: Budgeted Strong Community Search in Heterogeneous Graphs

statements.text: 1 (Meta-path). A meta-path 𝑃 is a sequence of node types defined over the schema 𝑇𝐺 = (A, E) of a heterogeneous graph 𝐺. It is represented as 𝑃 = ⟨𝐴1, . . . , 𝐴𝐿 ⟩, where 𝐿 = |𝑃 | is the length of the meta-path, and 𝐴𝑖 ∈ A for 𝑖 = 1, . . . , 𝐿. The types 𝐴1 and 𝐴𝐿 are called the starting type and ending type, respectively.
The optimization version of the BSC problem is not in APX for any 𝐷 [𝐴0 ] ≥ 4, unless 𝑃 = 𝑁 𝑃.
The Maximum Community Search (MCS) problem, which is the optimization version of the BSC problem, is not in PTAS when the degree threshold of anchor-type nodes satisfies 𝐷 [𝐴0 ] ≥ 4, unless 𝑃 = 𝑁 𝑃.
The union of two overlapping StrComs with consistent meta-path and constraints, forms a valid StrCom.
Given an instance of the BSC problem with query node 𝑞, the BSC is a subgraph of the maximum StrCom containing 𝑞.
When the meta-path’s length is 3 or 4, the upper bound on the P-support is equal to the exact P-support.

proofs.text: We prove the NP-hardness by reducing the 𝑘-clique [16] problem. The details of the proof can be found in the appendix. □

The optimization version of the BSC problem, referred to as the minimum strong community (MSC), aims to find the strong community that contains the query node and has the minimum number of anchor-type nodes. To prove the theorem, we give an L-reduction [5] from Minimum Subgraph of Minimum Degree (MSMD𝑑 ) [1, 2] to an instance of MSC problem in polynomial time. Given a graph 𝐺 = (𝑉 , 𝐸) and a degree threshold 𝑑, the goal of MSMD𝑑 is to find a subgraph 𝐻 ⊆ 𝑉 , such that (a) the degrees of every node in 𝐻 are larger than or equal to 𝑑, and (b) the size of the subgraph 𝐻 is minimized. MSMD𝑑 is a minimization problem and is not in APX, when 𝑑 ≥ 3. Given an instance of MSMD𝑑 (𝐺 = (𝑉 , 𝐸), 𝑑), we construct a heterogeneous graph 𝐺 ′ = (𝑉 ′, 𝐸 ′ ) by adding a node 𝑣𝑞 to 𝑉 and connect it to all other nodes, i.e., 𝑉 ′ = 𝑉 ∪{𝑣𝑞 }, 𝐸 ′ = 𝐸∪{(𝑣𝑞 , 𝑣)|∀𝑣 ∈ 𝑉 }. Every node in 𝑉 ′ is associated with the same type 𝐴0 . In the corresponding MCS instance, we set 𝑃 = ⟨𝐴0, 𝐴0 ⟩ as the meta-path, 𝑣𝑞 as the query node, 𝑘 = 1 and 𝐷 = [1] as the P-score and degree thresholds, respectively. Specifically, in the MSMD𝑑 intance, 𝑑 ≥ 3 and 𝑂𝑃𝑇 (𝑥) is no smaller than 4. Thus, Inequality 1 holds as 𝑂𝑃𝑇 (𝑥) + 1 = 𝑂𝑃𝑇 (𝑓 (𝑥)) ≤ 2 · 𝑂𝑃𝑇 (𝑥). Since MSMD𝑑 is not in APX for 𝑑 ≥ 3, MSC problem is also not in APX for 𝐷 [𝐴0 ] ≥ 4, where 𝐷 [𝐴0 ] is the degree threshold for the anchor-type node. □
